subject: FinPay MAP: performance test plan, throughput results & next-step commit
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: FinPay MAP: performance test plan, throughput results & next-step commit

Hi Alice / Tim —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our MAP, attached is an updated test plan and the initial throughput run we completed against your sample traffic shape. High level: we validated sustained QPS targets for the 8k-seq path and measured tokens/sec across the steady-state window.

Attachments: FinPay_MAP_v1.3.pdf (MAP + eval timeline), throughput-results-20260331.csv (raw logs), unit-econ-summary-3p31.xlsx (cost per 1M tokens / projected monthly spend).

Quick highlights from the run (details in attached CSV):
- 99th percentile TTFT (time-to-first-token) against the 8k path: 38 ms (p99 measured at 100 concurrent sessions).
- Sustained tokens/sec (steady-state, 2 minute window): 14.8k tokens/sec per 8x A100 pool; linear scaling observed up to our test cap.
- Sustained QPS (short requests ~120 tokens average): 110 QPS at 100 concurrent workers; sustained over 10 minutes without degradation.
- Unit economics (approx): $0.45 per 1k tokens served in this config; projected monthly for FinPay baseline traffic: ~$19,000/mo.

Next steps we propose inside the MAP:
1) Short checklist for final acceptance testing (security questionnaire + perf-run on a masked production sample) — target by Apr 6.
2) One canary rollout on Dedicated capacity for 72 hours (we can schedule Apr 12–15).
3) Procurement / contract signature — if the canary looks good, target committed capacity onboarding by Apr 23.

Can you confirm availability for a 30-min acceptance call this week to sign off the security items and select the masked sample?

Cheers,
Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Senior Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0191
From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@finpay.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tim Campbell <tim.campbell@finpay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 31 Mar 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinPay MAP: performance test plan, throughput results & next-step commit

Thanks Jonas — this is great and exactly what we needed to decide. Quick questions after skimming the CSV and the unit econ sheet:

1) The tokens/sec number — is that aggregated across the whole GPU pool or per-GPU? We need to translate to our peak hourly ingress numbers.
2) For the TTFT numbers, can you provide the distribution (p50/p90/p99) for the 4k and 8k paths separately? Security team also wants the sample of headers you sent in the masked run (IP/blinding details).

We're available Thu 10:00–11:00 PT for an acceptance call. Procurement is ready to review a redline if the canary dates are firm.

Best,
Alice
Director, Product — Conversational Payments
FinPay
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 31 Mar 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinPay MAP: performance test plan, throughput results & next-step commit

Jonas — added the per-GPU breakdown and the p50/p90/p99 slices to a short appendix (see the Drive link in the MAP). Highlights to pull into the acceptance call:

- tokens/sec: 14.8k tokens/sec was measured at pool level for 8x A100. Per-GPU median throughput ~1.85k tokens/sec.
- 4k path p50/p90/p99 TTFT: 12ms / 24ms / 52ms.
- 8k path p50/p90/p99 TTFT: 16ms / 32ms / 38ms. (p99 variance driven by cold-cache tails during a small restart we saw at 00:06:12).

Also included a short unit-econ sensitivity table showing projected cost at 50%, 100%, 200% traffic. Key note: using lightweight quantization profile Q3 yields ~22% lower $/1k tokens with <1% quality difference on our eval prompts.

I'll be on the Thu 10:00 PT call. Sergio — can you confirm Dedicated pool sizing for the canary (we recommended 2x the baseline to eliminate noisy multi-tenancy effects)?

-r

--
Rishi Malhotra
Principal, Inference Optimization
Redwood Inference
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 01 Apr 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinPay MAP: performance test plan, throughput results & next-step commit

Confirmed — we can allocate a 16-GPU Dedicated pool (8x prod-equivalent + 2x buffer for burst) for the 72-hr canary. Expected performance: sustained 28–30k tokens/sec in steady window (linear from the measured 14.8k at 8 GPUs). Concurrency handling: we suggest 120 worker sockets to keep p99 TTFT under 60ms for the 8k path.

I'll prep the runbook for the canary (metrics to watch: TTFT p50/p90/p99, sustained qps, token loss/errors, cost burn rate). Will share the runbook link ahead of the call.

-Sergio
From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@finpay.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2026 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinPay MAP: performance test plan, throughput results & next-step commit

Thanks team — call was productive. Action items we agreed on (pulled from the MAP):

- Redacted production sample: FinPay will deliver masked payloads by Apr 5 (Alice).
- Redwood to run masked-sample throughput test and deliver raw CSV + summarized econ sheet by Apr 7 (Jonas / Rishi).
- 72-hr Dedicated canary window: Apr 12 09:00 PT -> Apr 15 09:00 PT (Sergio to provision and run).
- Procurement will send a DocuSign redline by Apr 9 for the committed capacity (timing aligned to successful canary).

Acceptance criteria for the canary (from the MAP):
1) p99 TTFT < 65ms for both 4k and 8k paths over the 72-hr window.
2) Sustained tokens/sec >= 26k in steady-state (2-minute sliding) with <0.5% dropped requests.
3) Monthly projected unit economics must remain within 10% of the Apr 7 submitted econ sheet.

We are aligned on dates; procurement will follow up on the DocuSign. Looking forward to the canary.

Best,
Alice
